newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TWO SENT OFF AS RANGERS BEAT CELTIC.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-TWO SENT OFF AS RANGERS BEAT CELTIC.

text.p: Rangers took a huge step towards their ninth successive Scottish League title when they beat arch-rivals Celtic 1-0 at Celtic Park on Sunday thanks a scrambled 44th minute goal from Brian Laudrup.

But Rangers' victory in a tense, scrappy Old Firm derby game, was marred by the 67th minute dismissal of Mark Hateley, playing in his first match since his surprise return to the club from Queens Park Rangers on Friday.

The 35-year-old former England striker was shown the red card by referee Hugh Dallas after appearing to butt Celtic goalkeeper Stewart Kerr -- after Rangers had been awarded a free-kick for an earlier infringment.
Celtic also finished the match with 10 men when Malky Mackay was sent off in the 80th minute for hauling down Laudrup.
But Rangers, with six regular first team players missing through illness or injury, ended the afternoon on a high, moving eight points clear of Celtic with only six matches to play.
The only goal was a scappy one and came about after Ian Durrant lobbed goalkeeper Kerr from the left-hand side of the penalty area after a short back pass to the keeper from Alan Stubbs.
With Kerr well out of position, Laudrup and Mackay both chased after the loose, bouncing ball, and Laudrup forced it in off the post just ahead of Mackay's interception.

Laudrup had scored the only goal of the game when Rangers beat Celtic 1-0 here in November and his effort on Sunday took Rangers within touching distance of equalling the record of nine successive titles achieved by Celtic between 1965 and 1974.
